Build ein_relation from Schedule R and the group exemption structure

Source: R/md-ingest-relations.R
md_ingest_relations.Rd

Section 10 is emphatic that group and related-entity structure belongs in a relation table rather than the name table: group subordinates and affiliate chapters are distinct EINs with near-identical names, which is precisely the condition that produces false matches. Registering "BOYS AND GIRLS CLUB OF SPRINGFIELD" as an alias of the national EIN would make disambiguation worse, not better.

Usage

md_ingest_relations(version = "v2_2", con = NULL, bmf_version = NULL)

Arguments

version

Pinned efile_related version.

con

A connection from md_db().

bmf_version

The bmf_unified version the group edges are read from. NULL reads it from source_vintage: the version that loaded entity.

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

Details

matchdb's job is to record the relation with provenance. What to do with it - collapse, veto, or ignore - is a matching decision and lives in pfmatch (R/dyads.R, R/affiliation.R).

Self-references are dropped, and that is not the same as worthless

4,133 filers list their own EIN as a related organisation. An edge from an entity to itself is meaningless as a graph edge and distorts every degree statistic computed over the table, so they are dropped and counted.

But the first version of this note claimed they "carry no information", and that was wrong. Checked against the filer's own BMF name, 61.7% of self-references disclose a DIFFERENT name under the same EIN, and the examples are exactly the cases where IRS reporting structure and operating reality diverge:


  BACKBONE HOUSING INC          -> Backbone Housing Inc (dba Starner Hill)
  FRANCISCAN HEALTH SYSTEM      -> Franciscan Health System FKA Franciscan ...
  EMBANKMENT SERVICES INC       -> EMBANKMENT SERVICES INC (ESI)
  AMERICAN POSTAL WORKERS UNION -> APWU EMPLOYEES' RETIREMENT 401K PLAN
  ALABAMA SCHOOL OF FINE ARTS FOUNDATION -> Alabama School of Fine Arts
  Catalight Foundation          -> Impact Together

Those are DBAs, former names, acronyms, and genuinely distinct programmes operating under one exemption - a parish and its school, a foundation and the school it supports, a union and its benefit plan. Real information, and the kind a matcher wants.

It is not lost by dropping the edge, because what is useful about it is a name, and names are not this function's job. md_ingest_schedr() already writes every Part II counterparty name as an observed variant on the counterparty's EIN - which for a self-reference is the filer's own EIN. Measured: 4,116 of the 4,133 (99.6%) are already registered there. The edge is redundant; the alias is not, and it survives.

relation_raw carries the controller, not the activity

An earlier version put SR_02_RLTD_ORG_PRIMARY_ACT here, so Part II's raw values read HOSPITAL, HEALTHCARE, low-inc hsng, FUNDRAISING. That is the counterparty's activity - a property of the organisation, not of the relation - and §4 reserves relation_raw for the source's own wording of the relation.

On this form that is the direct controlling entity, with an explicit N/A where the filer states there is none. Population across 2009-2024:


  rows                        6,540,823
  direct controlling entity   4,501,572  (68.8
  explicit 'N/A'                950,837  (14.5
  primary activity            6,226,371  (95.2

Losing the activity costs nothing here, and only here: Part II counterparties are exempt organisations by definition and 119,865 of 119,865 (100%) resolve into entity, so each one's activity is available from its own record. That is not true of Parts III and IV, whose counterparties resolve at 5-9%.

controlled_512 is the sharpest signal the form carries

SR_02_RLTD_ORG_CTRL_512_X - is the counterparty a §512(b)(13) controlled entity - is a statutory yes/no, 93.1% populated (2.07M true, 4.02M false) against 68.8% for the controller name. It is what splits related_entity into controlled-by versus merely-related, and it is the only column on the form that answers that question directly rather than by inference from a name.

It is encoded four ways across schema versions - 0/1 and false/true - so both forms are normalised. Anything else becomes NULL: a blank box is silence, not a denial, and coercing it to FALSE would invent 449,599 assertions nobody made.

Aggregating to one row per pair uses bool_or, so a pair is TRUE if the filer asserted control in any year. The alternative - bool_and - would let one year with the box blank erase a control relationship stated in every other year.

Only Part II populates it. It is NULL for every other source, which is honest: no other disclosure asks the question.

Direction is fixed, not doubled

A relation row reads "ein_b is a relation of ein_a". Group rows are stored once as (central, subordinate, group_member) rather than also as the inverse group_parent, because storing both directions doubles the table to say nothing new. Consumers that want the reverse read the pair backwards.

Why group membership is not a clique

647,569 EINs carry a group exemption number, and 108 groups have more than a thousand members - one has enough that a member-to-member clique would emit hundreds of millions of pairs on its own. So membership is recorded as parent-to-member, which is linear in group size.

That requires identifying the parent, and the BMF affiliation_code does it. The codes are not ordered by seniority, which is a trap worth spelling out because an earlier version of this function fell into it:


  1  NETWORK-PARENT            parent, no group exemption
  2  NETWORK-INTERM            intermediate, no group exemption
  3  INDEPENDENT               unaffiliated
  6  GROUP-EXM-PARENT-REGULAR  parent of a group ruling
  7  GROUP-EXM-INTERM          intermediate within a group ruling
  8  GROUP-EXM-PARENT-CHURCH   parent of a group ruling, church or 501(c)(1)
  9  SUBORDINATE               subordinate in a group ruling

8 is a parent, not a subordinate. Reading the codes as ascending seniority puts 713 church parents on the member side of their own groups and never uses them as parents. Parents are therefore 6 or 8; members are 7 or 9.

Intermediates are deliberately treated as members only. A 7 is genuinely dual-role - a member of the central organisation and a parent to subordinates beneath it - but nothing in the BMF says which subordinates report to which intermediate, so emitting intermediate-to-subordinate links would be inventing a hierarchy the data does not contain. One level, honestly.

Groups with no coded parent produce no rows rather than a guessed one, and the count of those is reported.

Group exemption is not the whole of federated structure

Measured on the active BMF, a GEN and a group-exemption role are two encodings of one fact: no EIN carries a GEN without a group role, and only nine carry a group role without a GEN.

But 4,500 active organisations are coded 1 or 2 - network parents and intermediates with no group exemption at all. Affiliate structure does not require the group exemption process, and this ingest does not reach it, because a network has no GEN and therefore no key to join members on. This is exactly why the affiliate relation (§4a) is defined and holds zero rows. Worse, network subordinates are not separately coded - only nine subordinates lack a GEN - so those 3,459 network parents have members that cannot be identified from the BMF at all.

That gap is what Schedule R covers: disclosure does not depend on group exemption, so an affiliate relationship outside a group ruling still appears there. The two halves of this function are complementary rather than overlapping.

Schedule R gives both EINs, and sometimes only one

Part II lists related tax-exempt organisations with an EIN, so most rows resolve to a pair. Where the EIN is absent the row is still kept, with ein_b null and related_name carrying the counterparty as written - resolving a name to an EIN is a matching problem, which is npmatch's job, not something an ingest should guess at.
